---
title: "Access the Data With Stagecoach"
subtitle: "Link a versioned release into your analysis project"
execute:
  eval: false
engine: markdown
---

Use [Stagecoach](https://goldenplanetaryhealthlab.github.io/stagecoach/) to
symlink the shared releases into your own analysis project on FASRC. The
dataset is **not yet in the Depot**. Its current release directory is:

```text
/n/holylabs/cgolden_lab/Lab/frontier/works/prospectors/prospectorMDGHealthshedClinicData/data/outputs/releases
```

You can use a completed release without running the curation pipeline or
building its container. The [reader's guide](00_data-guide.qmd) explains the
files, joins, diagnosis definitions, and interpretation limits.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Prepare Your Analysis Project"}

You need an authorized FASRC account with read access to the shared release
directory and your own analysis project. A symlink uses your existing file
permissions; it does not grant access. Keep the shared release read-only in
your workflow and write analysis products in your own project.

Follow the [Stagecoach installation and project setup instructions](https://goldenplanetaryhealthlab.github.io/stagecoach/)
if needed. Run the following commands from your analysis project's root.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Declare the Shared Releases in Stagecoach"}

If your analysis project does not already have a `stagecoach_manifest.yml`,
create one:

```sh
stagecoach hail
```

Keep the generated Frontier, citizen, and project fields specific to your own
analysis project. In its manifest, enable `sources.01_gold_mine` and add the
following item to its `items` list. Merge this entry with any existing items.
This is a manifest excerpt, not a replacement for the full manifest:

```yaml
sources:
  01_gold_mine:
    enabled: true
    items:
      - name: mdg_healthshed_clinic_data
        path_regex: '/n/holylabs/cgolden_lab/Lab/frontier/works/prospectors/prospectorMDGHealthshedClinicData/data/outputs/releases'
        required: true
```

Stagecoach's `01_gold_mine` source supports FASRC symlinking from an explicit
readable path. Here it points to the Prospector's releases while the dataset
awaits Depot availability. Set `project.input_data_dir` to your analysis
project's `data/inputs` directory to use the paths shown below.

Inspect the manifest, resolve any reported issues, and stage it:

```sh
stagecoach inspect --manifest stagecoach_manifest.yml
stagecoach stage --manifest stagecoach_manifest.yml
```

Stagecoach creates the directory symlink at
`<input_data_dir>/01_gold_mine/<item name>/<source basename>`. With the
configuration above, your project sees:

```text
data/inputs/01_gold_mine/mdg_healthshed_clinic_data/releases
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Choose One Complete Release"}

List the available versions through the staged link:

```sh
ls data/inputs/01_gold_mine/mdg_healthshed_clinic_data/releases/
```

Choose a complete `v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<BUGFIX>/` directory containing
`datapackage.json` and its listed resources. The initial declared version is
`v0.1.0`; use it only once that package is complete and available. Directory
existence alone does not establish completeness. The current package defaults
to an internal candidate, so confirm that the chosen release is appropriate
for your intended analysis.

Record the explicit version in analysis code, together with the manifest
and release provenance. The symlink exposes the releases directory as it
changes; selecting a named version keeps the analysis tied to that version.
Use all tables from the same release. The
[reader's guide](00_data-guide.qmd#find-the-data-you-need) lists the resources
and shows how to load a diagnosis partition from this staged location.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Check the Link and Selected Package"}

For a completed `v0.1.0` package, run the following checks from your analysis
project. Substitute your selected version when needed:

```sh
test -L data/inputs/01_gold_mine/mdg_healthshed_clinic_data/releases
readlink -f data/inputs/01_gold_mine/mdg_healthshed_clinic_data/releases
test -r data/inputs/01_gold_mine/mdg_healthshed_clinic_data/releases/v0.1.0/datapackage.json
```

The resolved link should be the shared release directory printed above.
Before loading data, check that every resource listed in the selected
`datapackage.json` exists and matches its recorded checksum. Retain the
descriptor, version, and provenance in your analysis record.

:::
